prompt:
Draw a clean, top-down 8x8 chessboard (files a to h left to right, ranks 1 to 8 bottom to top, with small file/rank labels), squares in the usual alternating light/dark pattern.

IMPORTANT PIECE RULE: this uses a MADE-UP chess piece called the 'Skip'. The Skip does NOT move like a knight. From its square, the Skip can move to any square that is EITHER exactly TWO squares away DIAGONALLY, OR exactly THREE squares away in a straight line (horizontally or vertically). It cannot move any other way.

Place the Skip on square d5 (mark d5 clearly). Then HIGHLIGHT (fill with a bright blue colour) EVERY square the Skip can reach from d5 in one move under the rule above, and leave all other squares plain. Highlight exactly those reachable squares -- do NOT highlight the knight-move squares, and do NOT miss any reachable square. Do not print any square names or other text besides the small a-h / 1-8 edge labels.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a chess/checkers BOARD (an 8x8 grid of alternating light and dark squares) with some squares highlighted. Ignoring which squares are highlighted and ignoring artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT such a checkered board? A clean diagram counts as yes. Answer NO only if it shows a blank card, a plain panel printing text, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.
